title: Hold nothing back
takeaway: A true lover would rather be hurt by the beloved than ignored.
scene: The poet speaks to a beloved who has been 'killing' him with indifference and sharp looks. Instead of begging for mercy, he dares them to go on.

original: اَج چنے وی ہین ارمان دل دے، پورے کر لے قاتلا رہ نہ جان
کوئی وار تیرا میں تے روکنا نئیں، چڑھے ہوئے تیرے جوش لہہ نہ جان
transliteration: Ajj jinne vi hain armaan dil de, poore kar le qaatila reh na jaan
Koi vaar tera main te rokna nahin, charhe hoe tere josh leh na jaan
translation: Today, my killer, fulfil every wish your heart has, so none is left undone.
I won't block a single blow of yours; just don't let your passion cool.
couplets.story: He calls the beloved his 'killer' and says: go ahead, do whatever you want to me today. He won't try to stop any of it. His only fear is that the beloved will lose interest.

original: پھٹ لگڑے ایس لئی نئیں سیندا، مونہہ پھٹ نیں بڑے ہی زخم میرے
وجے ہوئے جو تکھے نیں تیر تیرے سخت جاناں والے ایہہ سہہ نہ جان
transliteration: Phatt lagre is layi nahin seenda, moonh-phatt nain bare hi zakhm mere
Vajje hoe jo tikkhe nain teer tere, sakht-jaanaan vaale eh seh na jaan
translation: I don't stitch up my wounds because they're so outspoken:
they'd tell how sharp your arrows were, more than even the toughest could bear.
couplets.story: He leaves his wounds open on purpose. Wounds can 'talk', he says. If people saw them, they'd see how sharp the beloved's arrows were, sharp enough to break even the toughest person.

original: مینوں پتہ اے تینوں پیار ہے وے پر ڈردیاں جھکدیاں پچھ دا نئیں
جنے محل اسارے نے حسرتاں دے تیری نہ پاروں ایہہ ڈھیہ نہ جان
transliteration: Mainu pata ae tainu pyaar hai ve, par dardiyaan jhakdiyaan puchh da nahin
Jinne mahal usaare ne hasrataan de, teri naa paaron eh dhaih na jaan
translation: I know you love me, but I'm too shy and afraid to ask,
in case all the palaces of hope I've built come crashing down at your 'no'.
couplets.story: Deep down he believes the beloved loves him. But he's too scared to ask. He's built up so many hopes, like palaces in the air, and one 'no' would knock them all down.

original: کسے نال پیار سوال کیتا، پیدل سیر نوں آپ کیوں نئیں آوندے
نقش پا میرے عاشق ویکھ کے تے کتے پا جھکیاں بہہ نہ جان
transliteration: Kise naal pyaar savaal keeta, paidal sair nu aap kyon nahin aaunde
Naqsh-e-paa mere aashiq vekh ke te kitte paa jhukiyaan beh na jaan
translation: Someone lovingly asked, 'Why don't you come out for a walk?'
'In case my lovers see my footprints and sit down bowing over them.'
couplets.story: Someone asked the beloved why they never go out for a walk. The answer is funny. If they did, their lovers would find their footprints and kneel down in the road to bow to them.

original: اک وار ٹکرا جو حشر ہویا، حشر تیک نئیں بھلنا رب دی سونہہ
اکثر بچ بچا کے لنگھناواں کتے فیر مڑ کے اکھاں کھیہ نہ جان
transliteration: Ik vaar takra jo hashr hoya, hashr teek nahin bhulna Rab di saunh
Aksar bach bacha ke langhnaavaan, kitte pher mur ke akhaan kheh na jaan
translation: What happened the one time we collided, I swear by God I won't forget till Judgment Day.
So I mostly slip past carefully, in case our eyes clash again.
couplets.story: They bumped into each other once, and it was like the end of the world. He swears he'll never forget it. Now he sneaks past carefully, scared that if their eyes meet again it'll happen all over.

original: تیرے عشق دا دل تے داغ گوڑا، جہنوں موت وی نئیں مٹا سکدی
وعدے پیار دے اساں توں بعد کدھرے تیرے دل دماغ توں لہہ نہ جان
transliteration: Tere ishq da dil te daagh goorha, jinhu maut vi nahin mita sakdi
Vaade pyaar de asaan ton baad kidhre tere dil dimaagh ton leh na jaan
translation: Your love has left a mark on my heart so deep that even death can't erase it.
I only hope that after I'm gone, love's promises don't slip from your heart and mind.
couplets.story: Loving the beloved has left a mark on his heart so deep that not even death can remove it. His only worry is the other way round: after he dies, will the beloved forget the promises they made?

original: اوہ اج کل میرے رقیب کولوں خوشخطی دی لین اصلاح جاوے
اوہدی دل دی تختی تے میرے ولوں لیکاں ہور کجھ پٹھیاں دیہہ نہ جان
transliteration: Oh ajj kal mere raqeeb kolon khushkhati di lain islaah jaave
Ohdi dil di takhti te mere valon leekaan hor kujh putthiyaan deh na jaan
translation: These days he goes to my rival for lessons in fine handwriting.
I just hope that, on the slate of his heart, a few more lines aren't written crooked against me.
couplets.story: He ends with a clever joke. Lately the beloved has been taking 'handwriting lessons' from the poet's rival, meaning spending time with them. The poet worries the rival will teach the beloved to write bad things about him on the 'slate' of their heart.

original: بھاویں جسم وچوں نکل جان روحاں، پر نئیں جانیاں کوفتاں ہجر دیاں
جدوں تیک لاشے تیرے عاشقاں دے تیرے پیراں دے تھلے گھہ نہ جان
transliteration: Bhaaven jism vichon nikal jaan roohaan, par nahin jaaniyaan koftaan hijr diyaan
Jadon teek laashe tere aashiqaan de tere pairaan de thalle ghah na jaan
translation: Souls may leave their bodies, but the torments of separation won't leave,
not until your lovers' corpses are trampled to dust beneath your feet.
couplets.story: Even dying won't end the pain of being apart. The ache will stay until the lovers have been ground into the dust at the beloved's feet. Only then is it over.

original: ذکر فکر توں یار محبتاں دا احمدؔ دل دے وچ لکائی رکھیں
تیری لگن وچ تیرے سجناں دے کتے اکھیوں اتھرو وہہ نہ جان
transliteration: Zikr fikr ton yaar mohabbataan da Ahmad dil de vich lukaai rakheen
Teri lagan vich tere sajnaan de kitte akhiyon athru veh na jaan
translation: Ahmad, keep your remembrance and your thoughts of love hidden in your heart,
so that, in their devotion to you, your loved ones' eyes don't spill over with tears.
couplets.story: He gives himself one last piece of advice. Keep your love and your remembering private, Ahmad, hidden in your heart. If you let it show, the people who love you will start crying too.

deeper: In Sufi thought, even hardship from God is a kind of attention, and being ignored would be worse. 'I won't block a single blow, just don't let your passion cool' is the seeker welcoming every trial as long as it keeps him near the Beloved. A mark on the heart 'that even death can't erase' is the Sufi belief that real love for God carries on into the next life.
why: The poem is full of wit: footprints people bow to, handwriting lessons from a rival. It shows that deep feeling and humour can sit side by side.
prompt: Is there something you care about so much you'd rather struggle with it than give it up?
notes: Several lines on this page are hard to read and use rare words. The overall sense is clear, but couplets 2, 4 and 7 should be checked by a native reader.
Couplet 7: 'khushkhati di islaah' means having one's calligraphy corrected, a traditional schoolroom image.
The last two couplets continue at the top of page 20.
